content:
The test image shows a tomato **leaf** with numerous small to medium dark brown/black circular spots scattered across a yellowing leaf. Key features:
- Multiple dark circular spots, some with slightly lighter centers
- General leaf yellowing (chlorosis)
- Dense spot distribution across the leaf
- Spots appear relatively uniform in size

Top candidates: Septoria Leaf Blotch, Bacterial Speck of Tomato, or Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus.

Now viewing one reference image to confirm:

Comparing the Septoria reference to the test image:
- Septoria reference shows circular spots with dark brown borders and tan/gray lighter centers (pycnidia visible)
- Test image shows similar circular dark spots, though somewhat more densely distributed with more leaf yellowing

The test image spots match Septoria Leaf Blotch well: circular spots with dark perimeters, small dark pycnidia in centers, no concentric rings (ruling out Early Blight), and yellowing around/between lesions. The high spot density and leaf yellowing are consistent with advanced Septoria infection.
